title: Records for Victor and with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: She recalls Man of War Blues and the sessions with Jelly Roll Morton, who knocked at the door during a take.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: What about Man of War blues and electrician blues?
Well, that was on the Victor.
Don't Throw It My Key Away is another one.
That is with Jelly Roll Morton. Well, this is fine.

On Victor. But no, the Man of War was with Leroy Smith's piano player. What's his name? Let me see. If I can think of his name. Oh, I don't remember his name. He was a piano player playing with Leroy Smith's orchestra. Leroy Smith was playing then at the time at Shuffle Inn.
Well, we'll look it up later. I got it probably in a bucket home.
Now, you did make records with Jelly Roll, though. I know you told me about that.
Oh, Lord, yeah. Don't Tell Me Nothing About My Man. And I Think I Hate a Man Like You.
And Jelly Roll took that other voice in there.
Yes. Yeah. He knocked on the door and said, Lizzy, come see your man going down the street with Fanny Bryce. Or Fanny something. Jelly was quite a fella.
